metadata.title: Education in the Eastern Partnership: Findings from PISA (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses PISA 2022 microdata collected through a two-stage sampling design within each participating education system: schools are sampled first and then students within sampled schools. The PISA target population is 15-year-olds enrolled in Grade 7 or higher, with countries allowed to exclude up to 5% of the target population under PISA technical standards; the report flags systems where sampling standards were not met (notably under COVID-19 disruptions and, for Ukraine, war-related participation constraints). The report does not specify the exact PISA weight variable names (e.g., student sampling weights) or whether replicate weights were used, so analysts should consult the PISA 2022 technical documentation for the appropriate weight and variance estimation variables. Because this is a descriptive policy report (not an ML model-training paper), weighting is primarily relevant for producing population-representative estimates and correct standard errors rather than for predictive model fitting.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report is a descriptive policy analysis of PISA 2022 outcomes (e.g., mean achievement, proficiency shares, and questionnaire-based indices such as belonging and safety) rather than an empirical ML study that explicitly models cognitive achievement using plausible values. As a result, plausible-value handling is not applicable to the extraction schema for PV-based achievement prediction. Missing-data handling is not reported at the level of an explicit analytic protocol (e.g., imputation vs. deletion rules) because the report focuses on high-level results and also notes specific non-response limitations for COVID-19 school-closure items, which affects representativeness for that module.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic focus is on PISA 2022 participants in the Eastern Partnership (EaP): Baku (Azerbaijan), Georgia, Moldova, and 18 of Ukraine’s 27 regions (those able to participate under war conditions). PISA targets 15-year-olds aged 15 years 3 months to 16 years 2 months at the start of the assessment period and enrolled in Grade 7 or higher; students outside the school system are not covered. The report also highlights that some systems did not meet PISA sampling standards in 2022 due to COVID-19 disruptions and that Ukraine’s participation involved a reduced regional coverage; comparisons across cycles are therefore restricted or interpreted with caution where the participating target population differs.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD/UNICEF report synthesizes PISA 2022 results for Eastern Partnership (EaP) education systems, focusing on student learning outcomes in mathematics (the core domain in 2022), reading and science; student well-being (sense of belonging and perceived safety); and expectations for education and work. PISA 2022 uses a two-stage sampling design within each participating system and assesses 15-year-olds enrolled in Grade 7 or higher; the report emphasizes that some systems did not meet PISA sampling standards due to COVID-19 and that Ukraine’s participation covered only 18 of 27 regions because of war. The report describes how PISA scores are interpreted (e.g., a 20-point difference approximates a typical annual learning gain) and how proficiency levels translate achievement into actionable task capabilities, including the baseline Level 2. Key descriptive patterns include EaP students trailing OECD averages, large shares of low performers, and substantial inequities by socio-economic status, alongside notable differences in belonging, safety, and educational aspirations. The report also cautions that COVID-19 school-closure questionnaire items have high non-response, limiting representativeness for those specific indicators.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is treated as a descriptive policy report rather than an empirical ML paper: the text provides assessment design, sampling participation constraints, and summary statistics/benchmarks, but it does not specify any predictive modeling pipeline, ML algorithms, or PV-based model estimation. Consequently, the schema’s ML-specific fields (ml_techniques and main_findings) are intentionally left empty, and confounder extraction is not performed because the report does not present a feature-based regression/ML specification. The main methodological emphasis is on PISA 2022 measurement and representativeness constraints (COVID-19 and war-related participation), which are handled through reporting cautions rather than through an explicit analytic protocol for PVs or missing-data imputation.
